newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-QBE still interested in acquisition.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-QBE still interested in acquisition.

text.p: QBE Insurance Group Ltd said on Monday it remained interested in making a significant industry acquisition but believed prices for many general insurance and reinsurance target companies remained too high.

"We have seen one or two things that we would have quite liked but frankly we thought shareholders would lose momentum in terms of the wealth that we were creating for them and we didn't want to do that," managing director John Cloney told reporters.
Cloney said the expansion strategy was not limited to Australia.
The company said in October last year that it could internally fund an acquisition of up to A$350 million.
However, Cloney said at a media briefing on Monday that QBE now had the resources to make a A$500 million takeover without resorting to outside funding.

While it was understandable that some shareholders might be disappointed at the failure to proceed with a large takeover, this was principally because "we were not happy with the prices that we would have to pay".
"I do not like to have a lot of goodwill on the balance sheet, I don't know how to make it pay," he said.
"We are still working on a few (acquisition) issues let me say. It sounds as though we have backed right out, we haven't.
"We are working on a few issues, they are not necessarily large but there are some things underway that might come to pass," Cloney said.
Without a substantial takeover, the role of Australia in the company's operations was likely to slightly diminish in the next two years, he said.
Australia accounted for 45.6 percent of gross earned premium in 1995/96, but this could fall to 40 percent, Cloney said, offset by growth in Asia and Europe.

"We will work hard to try and maintain a strong portfolio of Australian business in the future but I have to tell you that the things that look like bursting into bloom in the next couple of years of significant size, and even the generic growth, are all overseas," Cloney said.
Earlier on Monday, the company reported a 78.5 percent rise in 1995/96 net profit to A$147.3 million.

Gross earned premium rose 9.8 percent to A$1.49 billion, with Asia accounting for 19.2 percent of business, followed by Europe's 18.1 percent, North America at 9.8 percent and the Pacific on 7.3 percent. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
